output.summary: Cycad endemic to southern Western Australia, often growing trunkless in jarrah forests and bearing long, glossy, palm-like fronds. Its large cones contain seeds used as food by Indigenous Australians only after proper processing; unprepared seeds have caused severe poisoning.
output.edibilityNote: Properly processed seeds were an important Noongar food; unprepared seeds caused vomiting and poisoning. Processed trunk pith starch was also used as flour.
